memory_candidates.content: When a new PreToolUse Bash-matcher guard needs to detect a hazardous literal (e.g. a jq field name like 'active_projects') inside a shell command string, decide per-signal whether to scan the RAW command text or the quote-stripped COMMAND_SCAN text the git-family guards (guard-destructive-git.sh/guard-git-push.sh) already use. COMMAND_SCAN's quote-strip (sed -z 's/"[^"]*"/""/g') exists to avoid false positives from argv-STRUCTURE detectors (e.g. a commit message that happens to quote 'git commit --amend'). But a hazardous field name is almost always INSIDE a quoted jq filter argument (e.g. '.active_projects += [...]'), so scanning only COMMAND_SCAN for it produces a false NEGATIVE that silently defeats the detector's whole purpose. Fix: scan structural signals (redirect targets, mv/sed/tee shapes) against COMMAND_SCAN, but scan content-literal signals (a specific field/string that is expected to live inside quotes) against the RAW command. Verify any new Bash-matcher hook against its primary required case with a literal reproduction before trusting it, not just against synthetic unit fixtures -- a wrong default choice here passes shellcheck and a hand-built fixture suite but silently misses the real case.

A jq filter like `$newnums | index(.project_number)` inside a `map(...)` pipeline is a classic jq scoping bug: index()'s argument expression `.project_number` evaluates against index()'s OWN input (the array $newnums being piped in), not against the current map() element -- `.` inside `EXPR` of `arr | index(EXPR)` is `arr` itself, not the enclosing pipeline's `.`. This produces 'Cannot index array with string' or silently wrong results depending on shape. Fix: bind the needed scalar from the map element to a named variable BEFORE piping into index() -- `.project_number as $pn | ($newnums | index($pn))`. Separately, `$obj[EXPR]` (object bracket-indexing) raises 'Cannot index object with null' when EXPR evaluates to null (e.g. a missing/absent field read via `.field` with no `// default`) -- always guard with `(.field // "")` before using a read field as an object index, even when the field is 'always present' by the data model, since a test fixture or edge case will eventually violate that assumption.

When adding a new required-evidence gate to a shared, widely-called writer (e.g. state-write.sh's audit-evidence gate for new active_projects entries), proactively re-run EVERY pre-existing test suite that exercises that writer's creation path, not just the suites for the new feature -- a fixture that creates a record as SETUP for an unrelated test (e.g. a concurrency or payload-size test) will silently start failing once the new gate requires evidence it never provides. The fix is almost always a one-line addition (e.g. --audit-override "test fixture") to the fixture's own write call, not a change to the gate. Budget time for this sweep whenever a new gate's trigger condition (not its flag name) matches an existing writer's pre-existing, unrelated callers.
